solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mike cannot bat on unfortunately — he's not in action

indicators.note: something that turns out unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters before it are thrown out of order

parts.note: Mike is the radio alphabet word for M
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer called Mike sadly cannot carry on batting, so he is out of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash separates the wordplay from the definition; 'Mike' must be shrunk to its single letter before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A noncombatant is a person, such as a chaplain or civilian, who takes no part in the fighting.

clue.text: Growth area oddly abandoned? Correct, difficult to follow

indicators.note: says the word for difficult comes after the letters already built
the letters in odd positions are dropped, leaving only the even-placed ones of the next word

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word
hard means difficult

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a region of growth has been neglected, and is told yes, with hard times ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly abandoned' seems to qualify 'Growth area', but it acts on 'Correct' after the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot where fruit trees are grown, so it is literally an area of growth.

clue.text: In adroit way Conservative honest about Republican Party finally

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for honest wraps round the party letter

parts.note: level, as in 'on the level', means honest
R is the abbreviation for Republican

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A political profile praises a straight-talking Tory for their dealings with the Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: R sits inside LEVEL to make LEVERL, with C before and Y after.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleverly means skilfully or deftly, which is what acting in an adroit way amounts to.

clue.text: County of Prime Minister, old

parts.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A question about which county a former Prime Minister came from.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May led the UK government from 2016 to 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland.

clue.text: In skilful way introducing second pamphlet with theoretical approach

indicators.note: to introduce something is to bring it inside, so the word for in skilful way takes the others into its middle

parts.note: ably means in a skilful way
S is the abbreviation for second
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: A writer skilfully presents a second pamphlet arguing from theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link here; the container signal is 'introducing', which wraps the skilful-way word round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat something abstractly is to deal with it in theory rather than in concrete practice.

clue.text: Fruit from first-class firm, rather nice to begin with

parts.note: A is the top grade, as in A1
Co is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of each of the two words just before it

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A greengrocer praises the produce of a top-class supplier as fairly pleasant at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak tree, which botanically counts as a fruit.

clue.text: Animal more cheerful with time for new start

indicators.note: a new start means the opening letter is swapped out, with time put in its place

parts.note: merrier means more cheerful
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A pet seems happier once it has had time to make a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: The M at the front of MERRIER is replaced by T.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a small breed of dog, so an example of an animal.

clue.text: Figure of fun lacking guts, how almost completely awful!

indicators.note: almost completely means nearly all of the word is kept, its final letter lost
awful suggests something botched and messed up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how dreadful a cowardly person is, mocking them as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking guts' looks like a cue to drop middle letters, but both words are taken whole as anagram letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A laughing stock is a person everyone ridicules, so an object of mockery and fun.

clue.text: Referring to crisis not half threatening with nature of a counter-attack

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word survives, the back half being dropped

parts.note: re means concerning or referring to
the front half of the six-letter word
minatory is a formal word for threatening

explanation.surface: A report on a crisis that is somewhat menacing and has the look of a retaliatory strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Recriminatory remarks are accusations thrown back at an accuser, a verbal counter-attack.

clue.text: Transformative power of a Lima guerrilla leader that's surprising

parts.note: taken as written
Lima is the radio alphabet word for L
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Remarking on the surprising power of a guerrilla chief based in Peru's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like the Peruvian city, which fits a guerrilla, but it is just the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemy was the supposed art of turning base metals into gold, hence any magical transformation.

clue.text: Trouble from unexpected source that limits leader of Greens

indicators.note: to limit is to set boundaries around, so the rearranged letters enclose the next piece
unexpected suggests the word turns up in an unforeseen form, its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A political party's head faces problems from an unlikely quarter that hem them in.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a cause of great suffering or affliction, a serious trouble.

clue.text: To some extent hard-working lad engaged in clearing

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A diligent young man is busy clearing land, in part at least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clearing' reads as a verb for the lad's work, but it is a noun, an open space in a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A glade is an open space in a forest, which is what a clearing is.

clue.text: Border row after loud resistance, no turning back

indicators.note: after says the word for row is placed behind the letters that come before it

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical mark for loud
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: turning back means the little word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then read in reverse
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A noisy dispute at a border crossing, where resistance is met and no one turns back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as an argument, but here it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the border line between two countries.

clue.text: Regret of one travelling — arrival not right

indicators.note: not right means the letter standing for right is removed from the word before it

parts.note: a rep, a travelling salesperson, is always on the road
entrance, an arrival, loses one R

explanation.surface: A traveller is sorry that the arrival went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the usual abbreviation for right; it comes out of ENTRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Repentance is sincere sorrow for wrongdoing, a deep form of regret.

clue.text: Change clue ending as favour

indicators.note: an instruction to change the words means their letters are to be put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter is asked to alter the end of a clue as a kindness to solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: An indulgence is a privilege or concession granted, so a favour shown to someone.

clue.text: Daughter with unusual instrument

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
rum is British slang for odd or strange
simply joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: A girl takes up an uncommon musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' looks like an anagram signal but is the slang word rum, meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum is a percussion instrument struck with sticks or hands.

clue.text: Lethargy at home — a new tonic needed

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so these letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sluggish at home is told that a fresh pick-me-up is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction means doing nothing, the idleness that lethargy produces.

clue.text: Good copy — look in surprise

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to ape someone is to copy them

explanation.surface: A neat imitation makes people stare in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare open-mouthed, typically from wonder or amazement.

clue.text: One making undue fuss about Northern necklace?

indicators.note: about means around, so the fusser's word wraps round the letter for Northern

parts.note: a pedant fusses over minor details
N is the abbreviation for Northern

explanation.surface: Someone fussing about a piece of jewellery from the North.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a pendant is strictly what hangs from a necklace rather than the necklace itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is a jewel hung on a chain round the neck, so a kind of necklace by extension.

clue.text: Spooner's recounting was best for war leader

indicators.note: Spooner was a don famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the two words found here trade their first sounds

parts.note: telling a story is recounting it; it takes the opening sound of the other word
whoever won was best; it takes the opening sound of the other word

explanation.surface: Telling how the victory was won makes a story about a military commander.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Wellington defeated Napoleon at Waterloo in 1815.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellington commanded the British and allied army against Napoleon, a famous war leader.

clue.text: One raising glass that's found in the kitchen?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who proposes a toast, glass lifted
second meaning: an appliance for browning bread

explanation.surface: Someone lifting a glass at a party in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word names a person drinking a toast and the electric gadget that makes toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A toaster is both a person who drinks to someone's health and a kitchen appliance for grilling bread.

clue.text: Perseverance of Cardinal associated with an urban area

parts.note: a cardinal number is a counting number such as ten
the indefinite article, shortened
a city is a large urban area

explanation.surface: Praise for the persistence of a churchman tied to a big town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a church prelate, but it means a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is the quality of holding on stubbornly, which is perseverance.

clue.text: Official, old, coming round is excellent remedy from the outset

indicators.note: from the outset points to the opening letter of each of the words just before it

parts.note: the initial letters of the five words

explanation.surface: An elderly official arrives with news of a splendid cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' belongs to the definition: town criers belong to the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was a public official who once walked the streets calling out announcements.

clue.text: Continue without extra effort in seaside

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to keep moving with little exertion, as a car with the engine off
second meaning: the land along the shore

explanation.surface: Taking it easy on holiday at the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to proceed without trying, and the coast is the shoreline where land meets sea.

clue.text: Separate portion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to divide or move apart, as a verb
second meaning: a piece or section of a whole

explanation.walkthrough: 'Separate' reads as an adjective with portion, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To part is to divide or separate, and a part is a share or fraction of something.

clue.text: Maybe describing call from family group in port? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: the phrase reverses the stated relation, so the group goes around the harbour city rather than within it

parts.note: a clan is a family group
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A family gathering at a harbour sends out a summons, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' flips 'in', so the family group holds the port. 'Maybe' hints that clarion is just one word often used of a call.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarion call is a loud, rousing summons, so clarion is an adjective often used of a call.

clue.text: One piloting aeroplane initially by way of high point

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
via means by way of
a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone flying a plane heads up towards a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, a person who flies an aircraft.

clue.text: Event recollecting a recent entry? I don't think so!

indicators.note: re-collecting means gathering the letters up again and arranging them anew

parts.note: taken as written
surface padding: a scoffing aside that adds no letters

explanation.surface: An occasion that recalls something that happened lately, which the speaker scoffs at.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a three-hundredth anniversary marks anything but a recent happening, hence 'I don't think so!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tercentenary is a 300th anniversary, or the celebration of it, a special event.
